Subject: Payment method gatekeeping & marketplace interest — quick follow-up

Hi Natalie — great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and 2 requested confirmations so we can scope onboarding work and the commercial path.

Recap (short):
- Greenleaf is interested in a 3-month pilot for clinical-search summarization across 3 teams (~10 seats).
- Technical ok: no sensitive PHI in the initial dataset; procurement/security still needs standard evidence.
- Primary procurement constraint: AP tends to prefer PO-backed vendors for anything beyond routine SaaS card spend.

Could you confirm:
1) For a pilot at the scale discussed (~$18k initial spend), would AP allow payment via corporate card OR do you need a PO for the pilot?
2) Is Greenleaf open to procuring through a marketplace (e.g., your cloud marketplace or partner portal) if that speeds vendor setup?

Next steps I propose:
- If card is allowed: we proceed with a short SOW, pricing attachment and receipt-based billing; Redwood issues invoice at month-end.
- If PO required: we will produce a one-page SOW + vendor onboarding bundle (W9, insurance cert, SSQA evidence) and route a PO/contract.

I've attached a short onboarding playbook (Redwood_Greenleaf_Onboarding_Playbook.pdf) that lists required docs and a suggested timeline. Can you loop in the AP contact (procurement@greenleafmed.com) with a one-line confirmation on PO vs card by EOD Thursday? That will let Marissa/ I lock commercial terms.

Thanks — Vivek

--

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 9:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Natalie — great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and 2 requested confirmations so we can scope onboarding work and the commercial path.

1) For the ~$18k pilot: our default AP policy is PO for vendor relationships, but there is an operational exception for pilots < $20k if we route through the department card program and obtain a PO after vendor evaluation. So card is possible but requires written approval from the finance manager (I've looped procurement).

2) Marketplace: Greenleaf uses a limited set of partner marketplaces. If Redwood is in the Azure Marketplace or AWS Marketplace with pre-populated vendor info, our procurement team can often fast-track onboarding. Otherwise the manual vendor portal adds ~2–3 weeks.

What we need from Redwood to progress ASAP:
- Completed W9 (attached)
- Current COI / insurance cert (if available)
- Short pricing sheet and the SOW language for a month-to-month pilot (we can sign PO versus card based on finance approval)

I've attached our W9 (GF_W9.pdf) and added procurement@greenleafmed.com to the thread. Procurement team — can you confirm whether a card exception is likely for this pilot?

Best,

Thanks Natalie — and thanks for looping procurement. I want to outline two pragmatic commercial paths so Greenleaf can pick the low-friction option: 

Option A — Department card (fastest):
- Scope: 3 teams, month-to-month pilot, capped spend not to exceed $25k.
- Docs: SOW + invoice-based billing; we provide monthly invoices for reconciliation.
- Pros: Start in <5 business days after card approval.
- Cons: Requires an internal card exception email from finance, and we ask for a post-pilot PO if you want to continue.

Option B — PO route (enterprise-ready):
- Scope: same pilot but backed by a short PO + Redwood MSA addendum.
- Docs: One-page SOW + W9 + insurance + brief vendor questionnaire.
- Timeline: vendor portal + PO typically 7–15 business days.

Marketplace route: if Greenleaf can onboard via your cloud marketplace (we currently publish via AWS Marketplace private offers and have an Azure listing in pilot), procurement often reduces paperwork and shortens time-to-first-bill. Please let us know if procurement can accept marketplace procurement as equivalent to PO.

Attached is a compact pricing breakdown (Pricing_Tiers_2027.xlsx) and a suggested SOW paragraph that fits either route. If procurement signals card OK, we'll finalize the SOW and start the pilot intake. If PO, we will prepare the vendor bundle and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Deal id: RDW-8675 (for internal tracking).

Quick internal note on AP constraints and next actions so we don't miss the window:
- AP threshold: historically Greenleaf treats single-vendor card transactions up to $50k as eligible for the departmental/card program, but approvals require a finance approver email.
- PO runbook: Redwood should prepare (a) one-page SOW, (b) vendor onboarding bundle (W9, COI, insurance), and (c) a short security evidence checklist (SOC2 summary + contact). That speeds PO issuance.
- Marketplace: if procurement confirms marketplace acceptance, mark that as "expedite" on the deal and we can reduce required documentation.

Action items:

- Vivek: follow up with procurement@greenleafmed.com for the finance approver email so we can pursue the card exception.
